title: HR Employee Attrition Analytics Dashboard
tagline: SQL Server data modeling and Power BI analysis identifying where employee attrition risk and cost are concentrated
description:
I analyzed employee data for a company to figure out who was quitting and why. I found that new employees earning under $3,000 a month were leaving at more than double the average rate  38% versus 16% company-wide. I then calculated the actual cost of these exits by role, and found something managers wouldn't expect: the role with the most people quitting wasn't the role costing the company the most money a different, more senior role was. I put all of this into an interactive dashboard so managers could see exactly where the risk and the cost were, without needing to touch any code.

title: Autonomous Data Analysis Agent
tagline: Self-correcting AI agent that cleans messy datasets and generates analytical reports with zero human intervention
description:
Raw, real-world datasets are almost never clean, they arrive with inconsistent
date formats, missing values, duplicate records, and mixed-case or malformed
text, and cleaning them is typically a slow, manual, repetitive task.

This project solves that with an autonomous agent that ingests a raw CSV or
Excel file, inspects its own schema and data quality issues, writes and
executes its own Pandas cleaning code, and produces a stakeholder-ready
Markdown report, all without a human writing a single cleaning rule by hand.

The LLM client is provider-agnostic by design and was actually run against
three different providers (Anthropic, Google Gemini, Groq) during
development, proving the abstraction rather than just claiming it.

title: Football Recruitment Analyzer
tagline: Data-driven analysis revealing that clubs overpay for transfers with weak correlation (r=0.303) between transfer fees and on-pitch output with recommendations for performance-linked fee structures.
description:
This project analyzes 175,165 football transfers to answer: "Are clubs overpaying for transfers relative to what players actually deliver on the pitch?"

Key Finding: Transfer fee and attacking output (goals + assists) have only a weak 0.303 correlation, meaning clubs pay substantial premiums that poorly predict player performance. Examples range from Erling Haaland's exceptional EUR 1.18M per goal contribution to Miralem Pjanic's zero return on a EUR 60M Barcelona transfer.

Solution: Recommended performance-linked add-ons for high-fee signings instead of fully guaranteed upfront payments, backed by quantitative evidence of poor fee-to-output predictability.
